You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# handlr

Manage your default applications with ease using handlr!

Features

- Set default handler by extension or mime-type
- Intelligent mime type detection from files based on extension and content
- Open multiple files at once
- Set multiple handlers for mime/extension and use rofi/dmenu to pick one
- Wildcard support like `text/*`
- Automatically removes invalid/wrong `.desktop` entries from `mimeapps.list`
- Helper commands like `launch`, `get --json` for scripting needs
- Single compiled binary with no runtime dependencies

Usage

```sh
# Open a file/URL
handlr open ~/.dotfiles/pacman/packages.txt
handlr open https://google.ca

# Set default handler for png files
handlr set .png feh.desktop

# Set wildcard handler for all text files
handlr set 'text/*' nvim.desktop

# Set default handler based on mime
handlr set application/pdf evince.desktop

# List default apps
handlr list

# Get the handler for a mime/extension
$ handlr get .png
feh.desktop

# Launch a handler with given path/URL
handlr launch x-scheme-handler/https -- https://google.ca
```

Installation

- Install via your distribution's package manager if available (e.g., your distro's package named `handlr`).
- Download the latest release binary from the project's releases page and place it somewhere in your `$PATH`.
- To enable shell completions, install the appropriate completion files for your shell (place them in your shell's completions directory).

For more details, consult the project's releases and the binary distribution provided by the maintainers.

"""Formatting of command-line errors and operating-system failures."""
import errno
import json
import os
import sys


def quote(value):
    # Debug strings, as used in diagnostics, have double-quoted escapes.
    return json.dumps(str(value), ensure_ascii=False)


class Failure(Exception):
    def __init__(self, text, code=1, stdout=False):
        super().__init__(text)
        self.text = text
        self.code = code
        self.stdout = stdout


def io_debug(error=None):
    num = getattr(error, 'errno', None) or errno.ENOENT
    names = {
        errno.ENOENT: 'NotFound', errno.EACCES: 'PermissionDenied',
        errno.EPERM: 'PermissionDenied', errno.EEXIST: 'AlreadyExists',
        errno.ENOTDIR: 'NotADirectory', errno.EISDIR: 'IsADirectory',
        errno.EPIPE: 'BrokenPipe', errno.EINVAL: 'InvalidInput',
        errno.EINTR: 'Interrupted', errno.EAGAIN: 'WouldBlock',
        errno.EADDRINUSE: 'AddrInUse', errno.EADDRNOTAVAIL: 'AddrNotAvailable',
        errno.ENOTEMPTY: 'DirectoryNotEmpty', errno.ENOSPC: 'StorageFull',
        errno.EROFS: 'ReadOnlyFilesystem', errno.ETIMEDOUT: 'TimedOut',
    }
    return 'Io(Os { code: %s, kind: %s, message: %s })' % (
        num, names.get(num, 'Uncategorized'), quote(os.strerror(num)))

"""Small, literal INI reader for association and desktop-entry data.

The names and values in these files are significant verbatim.  In
particular, spaces around '=' are not silently discarded.
"""
from errors import quote


class IniError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, source, offset, rule):
        self.source = source
        self.offset = offset
        self.rule = rule

    def debug(self):
        before = self.source[:self.offset]
        line_num = before.count('\n') + 1
        start = before.rfind('\n') + 1
        col = self.offset - start + 1
        end = self.source.find('\n', start)
        if end == -1:
            line = self.source[start:]
        else:
            line = self.source[start:end]
            if self.offset >= end:
                line += '␊'
        byte_offset = len(before.encode('utf-8'))
        return ('Error { variant: ParsingError { positives: [%s], negatives: [] }, '
                'location: Pos(%d), line_col: Pos((%d, %d)), path: None, '
                'line: %s, continued_line: None }') % (
                    self.rule, byte_offset, line_num, col, quote(line))


def read_ini(text):
    groups = {}
    current = groups.setdefault('', {})
    offset = 0
    for raw in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
        line = raw.rstrip('\r\n')
        if not line or line.startswith('#'):
            offset += len(raw)
            continue
        if line.startswith('['):
            if not line.endswith(']'):
                close = line.find(']')
                error_at = close + 1 if close >= 0 else len(line)
                raise IniError(text, offset + error_at, 'section_char')
            name = line[1:-1]
            if not name:
                raise IniError(text, offset + 1, 'section_char')
            current = groups.setdefault(name, {})
        elif '=' in line:
            key, value = line.split('=', 1)
            if not key:
                raise IniError(text, offset, 'name_char')
            current[key] = value
        else:
            error_at = len(line)
            if line.startswith(' ') and line.endswith(']'):
                error_at += 1
            raise IniError(text, offset + error_at, 'name_char')
        offset += len(raw)
    return groups

"""XDG directory selection and local preferences."""
import ast
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path
from errors import io_debug, unwrap_error, quote

DEFAULT_SELECTOR = "rofi -dmenu -i -p 'Open With: '"
DEFAULT_CONFIG = 'enable_selector = false\nselector = "rofi -dmenu -i -p \'Open With: \'"\n'

    value = os.environ.get(name, '')
    return value if os.path.isabs(value) else fallback

        if home is None:
            home = os.path.expanduser('~')

        self.config_home = absolute_env('XDG_CONFIG_HOME', os.path.join(home, '.config'))
        self.data_home = absolute_env('XDG_DATA_HOME', os.path.join(home, '.local/share'))
        data_dirs = os.environ.get('XDG_DATA_DIRS', '')
        dirs = [s for s in data_dirs.split(':') if os.path.isabs(s)]
        if not dirs:
            dirs = ['/usr/local/share', '/usr/share']
        self.data_dirs = [self.data_home] + dirs
        self.app_dirs = [os.path.join(d, 'applications') for d in self.data_dirs]
        self.mime_file = os.path.join(self.config_home, 'mimeapps.list')
        self.config_file = os.path.join(self.config_home, 'handlr', 'handlr.toml')
        self.enable_selector = False
        self.selector = DEFAULT_SELECTOR

    def load_preferences(self):
        try:
            path = Path(self.config_file)
            if not path.exists():
                path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                path.write_text(DEFAULT_CONFIG)
            text = path.read_text()
        except OSError as ex:
            unwrap_error('src/config.rs:63:31', io_debug(ex))
        except UnicodeError:
            unwrap_error('src/config.rs:63:31', 'Io(Custom { kind: InvalidData, error: "stream did not contain valid UTF-8" })')
        self._parse_preferences(text)

    def bad_toml(self, text, pos, kind, message='', key=None):
        before = text[:pos]
        line = before.count('\n')
        col = len(before) - (before.rfind('\n') + 1)
        value = ('BadTomlData(Error { inner: ErrorInner { kind: %s, line: Some(%d), '
                 'col: %d, at: Some(%d), message: %s, key: [%s] } })') % (
                     kind, line, col, len(before.encode()), quote(message),
                     ', '.join(quote(k) for k in (key or [])))
        unwrap_error('src/config.rs:63:31', value)

    def _parse_preferences(self, text):
        # Only the two public preferences influence execution.  Other TOML
        # data is accepted, allowing applications to keep their own settings.
        table = ''
        offset = 0
        for raw in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
            line = raw.strip()
            if not line or line.startswith('#'):
                offset += len(raw)
                continue
            if line.startswith('['):
                table = line
                offset += len(raw)
                continue
            match = re.match(r'\s*([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\s*=\s*(.*)', raw)
            if not match:
                first = re.match(r'\s*\S+\s*', raw)
                pos = offset + (first.end() if first else 0)
                found = 'an identifier' if pos < len(text) and text[pos:pos+1].strip() else 'eof'
                kind = 'Wanted { expected: "an equals", found: "%s" }' % found
                self.bad_toml(text, pos, kind)
            key, value = match.groups()
            value = value.rstrip('\r\n')
            if table or key not in ('enable_selector', 'selector'):
                offset += len(raw)
                continue
            token = value.split('#', 1)[0].strip()
            parsed = None
            typ = ''
            if token in ('true', 'false'):
                parsed = token == 'true'
                typ = 'boolean `%s`' % token
            elif token.startswith(('"', "'")):
                q = token[0]
                try:
                    if q == "'":
                        end = value.index("'", 1)
                        parsed = value[1:end]
                    else:
                        # JSON and TOML basic string escapes have compatible
                        # spellings for ordinary configuration values.
                        import json
                        parsed, end = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(value)
                    typ = 'string %s' % quote(parsed)
                except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
                    self.bad_toml(text, offset + match.start(2), 'UnterminatedString')
            elif re.match(r'^[+-]?\d+$', token):
                parsed = int(token)
                typ = 'integer `%s`' % parsed
            elif re.match(r'^[+-]?\d+\.\d+$', token):
                parsed = float(token)
                typ = 'floating point `%s`' % token
            elif token.startswith('['):
                typ = 'sequence'
            elif token.startswith('{'):
                typ = 'map'
            else:
                self.bad_toml(text, offset + match.start(2),
                              'Wanted { expected: "a value", found: "an identifier" }')
            good = type(parsed) is bool if key == 'enable_selector' else isinstance(parsed, str)
            if not good:
                expected = 'a boolean' if key == 'enable_selector' else 'a string'
                # Scalar type errors point just beyond their value.
                pos = offset + match.start(2) + len(token)
                self.bad_toml(text, pos, 'Custom', 'invalid type: %s, expected %s' % (typ, expected), [key])
            setattr(self, key, parsed)
            offset += len(raw)

variants=[base+extra for extra in ['Comment=\n','X=\n','Empty\n',' \n','\t\n',';comment\n',' #comment\n','\t#comment\n']]

        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/plain').stdout, 'a.desktop\n')

        self.call('set', '.TXT', 'a.desktop')
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', '.txt').stdout, 'a.desktop\n')
        self.assertIn('text/plain=a.desktop;', self.contents())

        self.call('set', 'text/*', 'text.desktop')
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/plain').stdout, 'text.desktop\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/unlisted').stdout, 'text.desktop\n')
        self.call('set', 'text/plain', 'exact.desktop')
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/plain').stdout, 'exact.desktop\n')

        self.app('system.desktop', mimes='text/plain;')
        self.app('added.desktop')

        self.assertEqual(self.call('list').stdout, EMPTY_TABLE)
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/plain').stdout, 'added.desktop\n')
        output = self.call('list', '-a').stdout
        self.assertIn('Added Associations\n', output)
        self.assertIn('added.desktop', output)

        self.call('set', 'text/plain', 'a.desktop')

                         '{"handler":"a.desktop","name":"My Editor","cmd":"/bin/echo two words before after"}\n')

        self.call('set', 'text/plain', str(path))
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/plain').stdout, str(path) + '\n')

    def test_selector(self):
        self.app('a.desktop', title='First')
        self.app('b.desktop', title='Second')
        script = self.write('select.py', 'import sys\nsys.stdout.write(sys.stdin.read().split("\\n")[-1])\n')
        self.write('config/handlr/handlr.toml',

        self.write('config/mimeapps.list', '[Default Applications]\ntext/plain=a.desktop;b.desktop;\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/plain').stdout, 'b.desktop\n')

        command, log = self.recorder()
        self.app('a.desktop', command=command + ' prefix %f suffix', mimes='text/plain;')
        self.call('launch', 'text/plain', '--', 'file one', 'two"quotes', '--flag')
        self.assertEqual(self.wait_for_log(log), [['prefix', 'file one', 'two"quotes', '--flag', 'suffix']])

        command, log = self.recorder()
        self.app('terminal.desktop', command=command + ' --terminal')
        self.app('a.desktop', command='/bin/echo %U', extra='Terminal=true\n')
        self.call('set', 'x-scheme-handler/terminal', 'terminal.desktop')
        self.call('set', 'text/plain', 'a.desktop')

        self.assertEqual(self.wait_for_log(log), [['--terminal', '-e', '/bin/echo', 'one two']])

        command, log = self.recorder()

        self.write('data/mime/globs2', '50:text/plain:*.txt\n50:text/markdown:*.md\n')

        command, log = self.recorder()

        self.call('open', 'unlisted-file')
        self.assertEqual(self.wait_for_log(log), [['unlisted-file']])

        self.write('data/mime/globs2', '50:text/plain:*.txt\n50:application/pdf:*.pdf\n')
        self.call('set', '.TXT', 'a.desktop')
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', '.txt').stdout, 'a.desktop\n')
        self.assertIn('text/plain=a.desktop;', self.contents())

    def test_wildcard_precedence(self):
        self.app('text.desktop')
        self.app('exact.desktop')
        self.app('system.desktop', mimes='text/plain;')
        self.call('set', 'text/*', 'text.desktop')
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/plain').stdout, 'text.desktop\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/unlisted').stdout, 'text.desktop\n')
        self.call('set', 'text/plain', 'exact.desktop')
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/plain').stdout, 'exact.desktop\n')

    def test_added_associations_and_system_apps(self):
        self.app('system.desktop', mimes='text/plain;')
        self.app('added.desktop')
        self.write('config/mimeapps.list', '[Added Associations]\ntext/plain=added.desktop;\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.call('list').stdout, EMPTY_TABLE)
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/plain').stdout, 'added.desktop\n')
        output = self.call('list', '-a').stdout
        self.assertIn('Added Associations\n', output)
        self.assertIn('added.desktop', output)
        self.assertIn('system.desktop', output)

    def test_system_user_override(self):
        self.app('same.desktop', title='User', mimes='text/plain;')
        self.app('same.desktop', title='System', mimes='image/png;', system=True)
        info = json.loads(self.call('get', '--json', 'text/plain').stdout)
        self.assertEqual(info['name'], 'User')
        self.assertNotIn('image/png', self.call('list', '--all').stdout)

    def test_json_command(self):
        self.app('a.desktop', title='My Editor', command='/bin/echo "two words" before %f after')
        self.call('set', 'text/plain', 'a.desktop')
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', '--json', 'text/plain').stdout,
                         '{"handler":"a.desktop","name":"My Editor","cmd":"/bin/echo two words before after"}\n')

    def test_absolute_handler(self):
        path = self.write('outside.desktop', '[Desktop Entry]\nName=Outside\nExec=/bin/true\n')
        self.call('set', 'text/plain', str(path))
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/plain').stdout, str(path) + '\n')

    def test_selector(self):
        self.app('a.desktop', title='First')
        self.app('b.desktop', title='Second')
        script = self.write('select.py', 'import sys\nsys.stdout.write(sys.stdin.read().split("\\n")[-1])\n')
        self.write('config/handlr/handlr.toml',
                   'enable_selector = true\nselector = "' + sys.executable + ' ' + str(script) + '"\n')
        self.write('config/mimeapps.list', '[Default Applications]\ntext/plain=a.desktop;b.desktop;\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.call('get', 'text/plain').stdout, 'b.desktop\n')

    def test_launch_argument_expansion(self):
        command, log = self.recorder()
        self.app('a.desktop', command=command + ' prefix %f suffix', mimes='text/plain;')
        self.call('launch', 'text/plain', '--', 'file one', 'two"quotes', '--flag')
        self.assertEqual(self.wait_for_log(log), [['prefix', 'file one', 'two"quotes', '--flag', 'suffix']])

    def test_terminal_handler(self):
        command, log = self.recorder()
        self.app('terminal.desktop', command=command + ' --terminal')
        self.app('a.desktop', command='/bin/echo %U', extra='Terminal=true\n')
        self.call('set', 'x-scheme-handler/terminal', 'terminal.desktop')
        self.call('set', 'text/plain', 'a.desktop')
        self.call('launch', 'text/plain', 'one two')
        self.assertEqual(self.wait_for_log(log), [['--terminal', '-e', '/bin/echo', 'one two']])

    def test_open_groups_by_handler(self):
        command, log = self.recorder()
        self.app('a.desktop', command=command + ' %U')
        self.write('data/mime/globs2', '50:text/plain:*.txt\n50:text/markdown:*.md\n')
        self.call('set', 'text/*', 'a.desktop')
        self.call('open', 'one.md', 'two.txt', 'another.md')
        self.assertEqual(self.wait_for_log(log), [['one.md', 'two.txt', 'another.md']])

    def test_open_url_normalization(self):
        command, log = self.recorder()
        self.app('browser.desktop', command=command)
        self.call('set', 'x-scheme-handler/https', 'browser.desktop')
        self.call('open', 'HTTPS://EXAMPLE.COM:443/a/../b?q=two words')
        self.assertEqual(self.wait_for_log(log), [['https://example.com/b?q=two%20words']])

    def test_file_url(self):
        command, log = self.recorder()
        self.app('a.desktop', command=command)
        self.write('data/mime/globs2', '50:text/plain:*.txt\n')
        self.call('set', 'text/plain', 'a.desktop')
        self.call('open', 'file:///tmp/file%20name.txt')
        self.assertEqual(self.wait_for_log(log), [['/tmp/file name.txt']])
        result = self.call('open', 'file://remote/tmp/file.txt', code=2)
        self.assertIn('Bad path: /tmp/file.txt', result.stderr)

    def test_magic_detection(self):
        command, log = self.recorder()
        self.app('a.desktop', command=command)
        self.write('data/mime/magic', b'MIME-Magic\x00\n[50:application/test]\n>0=\x00\x04DEMO\n')
        path = self.write('unknown-file', b'DEMO\x00\xff')
        self.call('set', 'application/test', 'a.desktop')
        self.call('open', str(path))
        self.assertEqual(self.wait_for_log(log), [[str(path)]])

    def test_no_magic_rules_empty_buffer_fallback(self):
        command, log = self.recorder()
        self.app('a.desktop', command=command)
        self.call('set', 'application/x-zerosize', 'a.desktop')
        self.call('open', 'unlisted-file')
        self.assertEqual(self.wait_for_log(log), [['unlisted-file']])

    unittest.main()
